naslov: Three Foundations of Good Conduct Towards a Believer

segmenti.tekst: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ نَحْمَدُهُ وَنَسْتَعِينُهُ وَنَسْتَغْفِرُهُ
segmenti.prevod: All praise belongs to Allah; we praise Him, seek His help and ask His forgiveness.

segmenti.tekst: وَنَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنْ شُرُورِ أَنْفُسِنَا وَمِنْ سَيِّئَاتِ أَعْمَالِنَا مَنْ يَهْدِهِ اللَّهُ فَلَا مُضِلَّ لَهُ، وَمَنْ يُضْلِلْ فَلَا هَادِيَ لَهُ
segmenti.prevod: We seek refuge in Allah from the evils of our souls and from our bad deeds. Whomever Allah guides, none can lead astray, and whomever He leaves astray, none can guide.

segmenti.tekst: وَأَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ
segmenti.prevod: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, Who has no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and messenger.

segmenti.tekst: أَرْسَلَهُ اللَّهُ بِالْحَقِّ بَشِيرًا وَنَذِيرًا وَسِرَاجًا مُنِيرًا لِيُنْذِرَ مَنْ كَانَ حَيًّا وَيَحِقَّ الْقَوْلُ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ صَلَّى اللَّهُ تَعَالَى عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَى آلِهِ الطَّيِّبِينَ الطَّاهِرِينَ وَأَصْحَابِهِ الْكِرَامِ الْهُدَاةِ الْمُهْتَدِينَ وَسَلَّمَ تَسْلِيمًا كَثِيرًا إِلَى يَوْمِ الدِّينِ
segmenti.prevod: Allah sent him with the truth as a bearer of glad tidings, a warner and a light-giving lamp, to warn whoever is alive (of heart) and so that the Word may be fulfilled against the disbelievers (Ya-Sin 36:70). May Allah the Exalted bless him and his good and pure family and his noble companions, the rightly guided who guided others, and grant him abundant peace until the Day of Judgement.

segmenti.tekst: قَالَ اللَّهُ فِي كِتَابِهِ الْكَرِيمِ يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقَاتِهِ وَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ أَمَّا بَعْدُ
segmenti.prevod: Allah says in His noble Book: “O you who believe, fear Allah as He deserves to be feared, and do not die except as Muslims.” (Al Imran 3:102). To proceed:

segmenti.tekst: Praise belongs to Allah alone, the Exalted, subhanahu wa ta'ala, the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of the Day of Judgement, the Lord of jinn and mankind, and blessings and peace be upon His Messenger, the beloved Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), upon his family, upon his companions, and upon all those who follow the path, the path of the Qur'an, the path of the Sunnah of Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam.

Dear brothers, respected members of the congregation, one of the greatest blessings that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, gives a person is to be a nursery of goodness, a source of goodness, so that in his presence the believers feel safe and at ease, and in his absence they are sure that his tongue will not touch them.
Islam, dear brothers, did not come only so that a person would pray, fast and give zakat, but also so that he would have beautiful character, akhlaq, good morals.
The Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: "The most complete of the believers in faith is the one with the best character."
Many scholars have spoken about the good conduct of a Muslim towards a Muslim. But Yahya ibn Mu'adh, rahimahullah, summed it up in a few points, in a few short points.
He says that this is how a believer can best benefit a believer: the first thing, he says, is that if you cannot benefit him, help him, then do not harm him.
Do not harm him. So if your brother wants to find a job, do not be – you or I – one of those jealous, envious people who will run him down at every step:

"He's not like that, he's like this, a layabout," and so on. Or if our brother wants to start some private business, do not be one of those who will call the inspectors on him, or [unclear], or anything else.
If you cannot, or if we cannot, bring our soul to accept that because of some [unclear] of ours or the malice that is within us, then at least let us not be among those who harm our brother.

If we cannot help him, let us not be among those who harm him. For the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: "The believer, the true believer, is the one from whose tongue and hands" – what? – "the other believers are safe."

The other believers are safe. By Allah, if the other believers are not safe from our tongue and our hands, then we are not believers. Then we are not believers; we have not understood Islam the way we ought to understand it.

The second thing, as Yahya ibn Mu'adh, rahimahullahu ta'ala, says: "If you cannot," he says, "make him happy, do not make him sad." Do not make him sad. Sometimes a person has some problems, loses his job, loses his marriage or something else, and he expects a kind word from a believer.

Believe me, sometimes when things get hard for a person, when he has a hard day, week, month, it is enough for him to meet a man he loves and respects who smiles at him and says a kind word to him – believe me, it can make his day.

Wallahi, it can make his day. And the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: "A smile to your believing brother is" – what? – "sadaqa (charity)." Sadaqa. So your kind word, your smile, can make a person's day. And not that we make him sad: "Well, you're to blame for that, you should have done it like this, you brought this and that on yourself…" – that you lost your job, that you lost your wife, and so on and so forth. Rather, the least you can do for a believing brother is to smile at him, and the most is to help him in some way, or to offer him [unclear]

a kind word. And the last thing Yahya ibn Mu'adh mentions, he says: "If you cannot praise him," he says, "do not disparage him." If you cannot praise him, do not disparage him. Believe me, dear brothers, it often happens that we have new members of the congregation, people who have only just started to pray, and when such a person comes to the mosque – look, these people have a certain feeling and a certain idea that in the mosque everyone is a companion of the Prophet, a pious devotee – and then, when he comes to the mosque, he does something that is not quite the custom of that mosque or that congregation.

And you will see some member of the congregation [unclear]: "Why like this, why like that, why this and that…" And then the man runs away, runs away from the mosque, leaves the mosque and never comes back. Why? Precisely because of these things. If you do not know how to praise him, if it is not in your power, if you are not very good at it, not eloquent, not good with words, then do not disparage him, do not say anything to him.
Just think, because with your disparagement you will do very great harm to that very brother who has only just come, come to pray in the mosque. These are words worth their weight in gold.

Worth their weight in gold. Whoever applies them in his life will find his life much better, because sometimes a person has no money to give in charity, he is not learned enough to advise others or to teach others, but the least he can do is not to harm his brother, not to scold his brother, not to bring sorrow into his heart.

That is the least, the very least, dear brothers, that we can do as believers, as Muslims. I ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to have mercy on us, to forgive our sins, to make us much better Muslims, to improve our situation in the Sandžak, to improve our situation in the world.
I ask Him, the Exalted, to bring us together in Jannah (Paradise).
آمِينَ يَا رَبَّ الْعَالَمِينَ بَارَكَ اللَّهُ لِي وَلَكُمْ فِي الْقُرْآنِ الْعَظِيمِ وَنَفَعَنِي وَإِيَّاكُمْ بِمَا فِيهِ مِنَ الْآيَاتِ وَالذِّكْرِ الْحَكِيمِ
segmenti.prevod: Amen, O Lord of the worlds. May Allah bless me and you through the Mighty Qur’an and benefit me and you with the verses and the wise reminder it contains.

segmenti.tekst: أَقُولُ قَوْلِي هَٰذَا وَأَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ لِي وَلَكُمْ فَاسْتَغْفِرُوهُ إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ
segmenti.prevod: I say these words of mine and ask Allah for forgiveness for myself and for you, so ask Him for forgiveness; truly He is the Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful.

segmenti.tekst: الحمد لله حمد الكاملين
segmenti.prevod: Praise be to Allah… (part not clearly recognised)

segmenti.tekst: وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى نَبِيِّنَا مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِهِ وَصَحْبِهِ أَجْمَعِينَ، تعظيما لنبيه وتكريما لفخامة شأن شرف الصفي، قال عز وجل من قائل مخبرا وآمرا
segmenti.prevod: And blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, his family and all his companions – in reverence for His Prophet and in honour of the lofty rank of the Chosen One. The Mighty and Majestic says, informing and commanding:

segmenti.tekst: إِنَّ اللَّهَ وَمَلَائِكَتَهُ يُصَلُّونَ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ ۚ يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا صَلُّوا عَلَيْهِ وَسَلِّمُوا تَسْلِيمًا اللَّهُمَّ بَارِكْ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ كَمَا بَارَكْتَ عَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَعَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ إِنَّكَ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ
segmenti.prevod: “Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who believe, send blessings upon him and greet him with peace.” (Al-Ahzab 33:56). O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim; You are indeed Praiseworthy, Glorious.
